title: Optimized method for differential gene expression analysis in non-model species
author: Aurelio, Fabián, et al.

steps.title: Combine raw read files
steps.instruction: Concatenate all cleaned forward reads into a single file named all_R1.fastq and all cleaned reverse reads into all_R2.fastq.

steps.title: De novo transcriptome assembly with Trinity
steps.instruction: Run Trinity (Docker version recommended) on the combined read files using fastq input, full cleanup, and output the assembly as Trinity_reference.

steps.title: Build Bowtie2 index for the assembly
steps.instruction: Create a Bowtie2 index from the Trinity assembly FASTA file.

steps.title: Align reads to the assembly with Bowtie2
steps.instruction: Map the combined forward and reverse reads to the Bowtie2 index using sensitive local mode, saving the SAM output and logging the run.

substeps.instruction: bowtie2 -x out_bowtie2_index -1 all_R1.fastq -2 all_R2.fastq --sensitive --local -S out.sam 2>&1 | tee result_bowtie2.log

steps.title: Assess assembly quality with BUSCO
steps.instruction: If Bowtie2 alignment rate is ≥70 %, run BUSCO in transcriptome mode using the embryophyta lineage; interpret BUSCO results, noting that homology values >80 % indicate good assembly quality.

description: Differential gene expression analysis constitutes the primary application of data derived from RNAseq sequencing. This methodological approach facilitates the identification of genes or transcripts that display differential expression in samples with significant contrasts. This process is essential for understanding gene regulation and biological responses to various experimental or pathological conditions [1]. RNA-seq data frequently encapsulates a multifaceted landscape of gene expression, influenced by a myriad of factors such as biological and technical noise [2,3]. This complexity is further amplified in non-model species, where comprehensive transcriptomic datasets are often lacking [2]. To address these challenges, our method concentrates on a curated panel of genes with known or hypothesized functions. It is crucial to note that this targeted approach does not imply the irrelevance of genes outside this curated panel. Rather, the method is designed to yield a dataset that is both manageable and interpretable, thereby facilitating the investigation of specific research questions.
